_about: Curated top picks for Lima's tourist districts (Miraflores, Barranco, San Isidro, Centro Histórico, Pueblo Libre, Surquillo). Coordinates are approximate (typically within 100–200 m) and are replaced by Google's exact location when a Google Places key is configured. Ratings always come from Google.

places.name: Hilton Lima Miraflores
places.notes: Home base. Parque Kennedy is a 5-minute walk north-west, Larcomar and the Malecón 10 minutes south.

places.name: Mercado de Surquillo (Mercado N° 1)
places.notes: The chefs' market, 15 minutes' walk from Miraflores: Andean potatoes, ají peppers, exotic fruit, fresh fish, cheap ceviche and juice stalls.

places.name: Mercado Central de Lima
places.notes: Huge and chaotic central market beside Chinatown; fruit, meat, Peruvian pantry goods and lunch counters. Keep valuables close.

places.name: Mercado Indio (Inka Market)
places.notes: Blocks of stalls with alpaca knitwear, silver, textiles and ceramics; bargaining expected.

places.name: Bioferia de Miraflores
places.notes: Organic producers' market: fruit, cheese, bread, honey and breakfast stalls, a short walk from the hotel.

places.name: Dédalo Arte y Artesanía
places.notes: Old mansion full of Peruvian designers' ceramics, jewellery and textiles, with a garden café at the back.

places.name: Mercado de Magdalena
places.notes: Local market famous for its ceviche and seafood counters at lunch; near Museo Larco.

places.name: Barrio Chino (Calle Capón)
places.notes: Lima's Chinatown: chifa restaurants (Peruvian-Chinese), bakeries and shops along Calle Capón.

places.name: Central
places.notes: Virgilio Martínez's tasting menu by altitude, ranked the world's best restaurant in 2023. Book months ahead.

places.name: Kjolle
places.notes: Pía León's restaurant upstairs from Central; easier to book, same produce, à la carte.

places.name: Maido
places.notes: Mitsuharu Tsumura's Nikkei tasting menu; top of the World's 50 Best in 2025. Reserve well ahead.

places.name: Astrid y Gastón
places.notes: Gastón Acurio's flagship in a colonial hacienda; lunch menu is the affordable way in.

places.name: La Mar Cebichería
places.notes: Acurio's ceviche house: classic ceviche, tiradito, chicharrón de pescado. Arrive before 13:00 to avoid the queue.

places.name: Isolina Taberna Peruana
places.notes: Huge sharing plates of old-school Lima food: seco de res, cau cau, offal done right. Go hungry.

places.name: Mérito
places.notes: Juan Luis Martínez's small, inventive tasting plates; one of Latin America's 50 Best.

places.name: El Mercado
places.notes: Rafael Osterling's seafood lunch spot; ceviches and the cangrejo (crab) dishes.

places.name: Rafael
places.notes: Rafael Osterling's elegant main restaurant; Mediterranean-Peruvian.

places.name: Mayta
places.notes: Jaime Pesaque's tasting menu with a serious pisco bar.

places.name: Cosme
places.notes: Relaxed, creative Peruvian plates; good cocktails.

places.name: Panchita
places.notes: Acurio's criollo restaurant: anticuchos (beef-heart skewers), lomo saltado, papa rellena.

places.name: Ámaz
places.area: Miraflores (Av. La Paz, beside the hotel)
places.notes: Pedro Miguel Schiaffino's Amazonian cooking: river fish, jungle fruit, patarashca. Right next to the Hilton.

places.name: Punto Azul
places.notes: Good-value ceviche and arroz con mariscos; big portions, usually a queue.

places.name: Al Toke Pez
places.notes: Tiny counter with a short daily menu (ceviche, chicharrón, combinado). Cash, queue, worth it.

places.name: La Picantería
places.notes: Communal tables; pick a whole fish from the ice and have it done two ways.

places.name: Canta Rana
places.notes: Football-memorabilia-covered Barranco classic for ceviche and seafood.

places.name: El Chinito
places.notes: Since 1960: the chicharrón sandwich with sweet potato and salsa criolla.

places.name: La Lucha Sanguchería
places.notes: Open late; the chicharrón or pavo (turkey) sandwich and fresh juices.

places.name: Siete Sopas
places.notes: Seven soups a day, 24 hours; the Sunday caldo de gallina cure.

places.name: Huaca Pucllana Restaurant
places.notes: Dinner looking onto the floodlit pre-Inca pyramid.

places.name: La Rosa Náutica
places.notes: Victorian-style restaurant on a pier over the Pacific; go for sunset drinks and the view.

places.name: Pescados Capitales
places.notes: Seven-deadly-sins-themed seafood menu; reliable ceviche and tiraditos.

places.name: Chez Wong
places.notes: Javier Wong cooks the day's sole in front of you; no menu. Taxi there and back.

places.name: Osaka
places.notes: Stylish Nikkei; sushi, tiraditos and a long pisco list.

places.name: Tanta (Larcomar)
places.notes: Acurio's all-day café with the greatest hits of Peruvian cooking and a cliff-top view.

places.name: Cala
places.notes: On the beach below the cliffs; good for a long lunch by the water.

places.name: Ayahuasca Restobar
places.notes: Pisco cocktails in a restored republican-era mansion; Barranco's best-known bar.

places.name: Carnaval
places.notes: Aaron Díaz's theatrical cocktails; one of the World's 50 Best Bars.

places.name: Juanito de Barranco
places.notes: 1937 bar with wooden counter, jamón sandwiches and cheap pisco.

places.name: Victoria Bar
places.notes: Next door to Central; cocktails and small plates in a historic house.

places.name: Lady Bee
places.notes: Peruvian-ingredient cocktails; on Latin America's 50 Best Bars.

places.name: Bar Inglés (Country Club Lima Hotel)
places.notes: Classic pisco sour in the wood-panelled bar of the 1927 Country Club hotel.

places.name: Bar Cordano
places.notes: Since 1905: pisco, butifarra sandwiches and presidents at the next table.

places.name: Tostaduría Bisetti
places.notes: Peruvian single-origin coffee roasted on site; garden tables behind.

places.name: Puku Puku Café
places.notes: Good Peruvian coffee and breakfast two blocks from the hotel.

places.name: Arábica Espresso Bar
places.notes: Small, serious espresso bar near Parque Kennedy.

places.name: Neira Café Lab
places.notes: Barista-champion café; pour-overs from small Peruvian farms.

places.name: El Pan de la Chola
places.notes: Sourdough, pastries and brunch; pairs with a La Mar lunch across the road.

places.name: Huaca Pucllana
places.notes: Adobe pyramid from AD 500 in the middle of Miraflores; guided visits only.

places.name: Parque Kennedy
places.notes: Miraflores' central park, famous for its cats; picarones and churros stalls in the evening.

places.name: Larcomar
places.notes: Shopping centre built into the cliff with terraces over the Pacific.

places.name: Parque del Amor / Malecón
places.notes: Gaudí-style mosaic park on the Malecón; paragliders launch from the cliffs nearby.

places.name: Faro de la Marina
places.notes: 1900 lighthouse on the Malecón; sunset viewpoint.

places.name: Puente de los Suspiros
places.notes: Barranco's wooden Bridge of Sighs; hold your breath crossing it for a wish.

places.name: Bajada de los Baños
places.notes: Old fishermen's path down to the sea, lined with bars and restaurants.

places.name: MATE – Museo Mario Testino
places.notes: Testino's photography in a restored mansion.

places.name: Museo Pedro de Osma
places.notes: Colonial art in a belle-époque mansion with gardens, opposite Central.

places.name: Plaza Mayor (Plaza de Armas)
places.notes: Government Palace (changing of the guard around noon), Cathedral and Archbishop's Palace.

places.name: Catedral de Lima
places.notes: Pizarro's tomb and the religious art museum.

places.name: Convento de San Francisco
places.notes: Catacombs with thousands of bones and a 17th-century library.

places.name: Plaza San Martín
places.notes: Grand 1920s square; Gran Hotel Bolívar's pisco sour is a classic stop.

places.name: Museo Larco
places.notes: Lima's best museum: pre-Columbian gold, textiles and the erotic pottery gallery, in a bougainvillea-covered mansion with a good café.

places.name: MALI – Museo de Arte de Lima
places.notes: 3,000 years of Peruvian art in an 1870s exhibition palace.

places.name: Circuito Mágico del Agua
places.notes: Illuminated fountain shows after dark; cheap and fun with kids.

places.name: Huaca Huallamarca
places.notes: Smaller restored pyramid among San Isidro's apartment blocks.

places.name: Bosque El Olivar
places.notes: Centuries-old olive grove; quiet walks and the San Isidro restaurants around it.
